advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Limit `_note_build_drift` to real degrades (e.g. require `coverage.llm_error` or an unsigned INDETERMINATE verdict) so reuse, inert and claimability verdicts are not annotated, and add a test for the reuse PASS case
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:268: if not isinstance(coverage, dict) or coverage.get("llm_ran") is not False:
src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:264: Only an unsigned, model-never-ran verdict is touched: its ``coverage.llm_error`` would
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:168: coverage: dict[str, Any] = {"llm_ran": False, "idempotent_skip": True}
advisory.finding: `_note_build_drift` annotates every verdict with `coverage.llm_ran is False`, not just provider-failure degrades. So the signed idempotent-reuse PASS, the BLOCK verdict-reuse, the inert disabled-gate PASS and claimability verdicts get a 'update the checkout ... then re-run the gate' remedy as well. The docstring says 'Only an unsigned, model-never-ran verdict is touched', but nothing checks the signature, an `llm_error`, or an INDETERMINATE verdict.
scenarios: An older build reuses a still-current signed plan-review PASS (idempotent skip). The PASS now carries build_drift telling the operator to update and re-run, even though nothing failed.
The code-review gate is disabled, so the inert PASS goes out. A behind build still attaches the drift remedy to it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Return early unless `coverage.get("llm_ran") is False and coverage.get("llm_error")` is truthy (or `result.get("verdict") == "INDETERMINATE"`). Make the docstring match the predicate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the remedy from the pinned sha (e.g. `git fetch origin && git checkout <pinned_sha>` / merge it) instead of hardcoding origin/main
evidence: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:250-252: "update the checkout running the gate to that ref (git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main) and run `make install`"
advisory.finding: The remedy hardcodes `git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only origin/main`, but the pinned ref is configurable (`REBAR_GATE_REF` / `[snapshot].ref`, or an explicit branch, tag or SHA). When the gate pinned anything other than origin/main, the suggested command does not move the checkout to the ref the note says to update to.
scenarios: A gate is run with ref set to a release tag or a feature-branch SHA that is not on main. The note tells the operator to fast-forward to origin/main, which may not contain the pinned commit or may go past it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Word the command in terms of the pinned sha, e.g. f"git fetch origin && git merge --ff-only {drift.pinned_sha}", or leave out the concrete command and just name the sha.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pop `_FOUND[pinned_sha]` on the exception path of `warn_if_behind` as well as on the `drift is None` path
evidence: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:199-201: except Exception: logger.debug(...); return None
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:205-208: if drift is None: if pinned_sha: _FOUND.pop(pinned_sha, None); return None
advisory.finding: If `detect_drift` raises, `warn_if_behind` returns before the `_FOUND.pop` cleanup, so an earlier drift entry for that pinned sha survives. A later degraded verdict in the same long-lived process (MCP daemon) would then name drift this resolution never proved. The new 'failure path' leaves a stale positive instead of clearing it.
scenarios: A dev-editable build is updated in place (running_build_sha reads the live checkout). The next resolution's probe raises, and the old drift entry stays and is attached to the next degraded verdict for that sha.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move the `_FOUND.pop(pinned_sha, None)` to run before `detect_drift` (or into the except arm) so only a fresh proven drift leaves an entry.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs the drift check as the old build and then as the pinned build in one process, and asserts the degraded verdict has no `build_drift`
evidence: src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:205-207: `if drift is None:` / `if pinned_sha:` / `_FOUND.pop(pinned_sha, None)` (added lines)
tests/unit/test_build_drift_degraded_verdict.py fixture: `build_drift.reset_warned()  # the recorded finding is process-global`, and reset_warned now does `_FOUND.clear()` (build_drift.py:260)
test_build_at_the_pinned_ref_adds_nothing calls `_resolve_as_build(monkeypatch, new[:11], root, new)` exactly once on an empty store, so the deletion has nothing to remove
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:199-201: when detect_drift raises, warn_if_behind returns None BEFORE the deletion, so an old entry survives; no test covers this either
test_a_verdict_where_the_model_ran_is_not_annotated and test_a_local_source_gate_pins_nothing_and_is_not_annotated assert only `assert "build_drift" not in result["coverage"]`
src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py:239: `drift = _FOUND.get(pinned_sha) if pinned_sha else None` (with sha None the result is None whether or not drift was recorded)
advisory.finding: The newly added deletion of old drift records (`_FOUND.pop(pinned_sha, None)` when a later check finds no drift) has no test that would fail if it were removed. `test_build_at_the_pinned_ref_adds_nothing` runs after the fixture has emptied the store, so `_FOUND` is already empty and the test passes with or without the deletion.
merged_from: The negative tests check only that `build_drift` is absent, and never confirm that the drift setup actually found drift: `_resolve_as_build` throws away what `warn_if_behind` returns. The local-source test passes no matter what the code does, because the record is saved under the full `new` SHA and the lookup uses `handle.sha=None`.
scenarios: In one process: warn_if_behind(new) as build=old (drift recorded), then warn_if_behind(new) as build=new (no drift), then annotate_result(degraded, handle(sha=new)). If the deletion regresses, the verdict wrongly carries build_drift telling the user to update and run `make install`.
Same sequence where the second detect_drift raises: the old record is never cleared and the verdict is wrongly annotated.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: `_resolve_as_build(monkeypatch, old[:11], root, new)`, then `_resolve_as_build(monkeypatch, new[:11], root, new)`, then `result = gate_source.annotate_result(_degraded(), SnapshotHandle(path=root, sha=new, source=SOURCE_ATTESTED))` and `assert "build_drift" not in result["coverage"]`. Optionally add a variant where the second check monkeypatches `build_drift.detect_drift` to raise.
